newsitem.title: ISRAEL: U.S.-held Hamas leader would go to third country.
newsitem.headline: U.S.-held Hamas leader would go to third country.

text.p: The leader of the Palestinian militant group Hamas - awaiting extradition from the United States - told an Israeli newspaper he would agree to be sent to another country instead of Israel.

In an interview from his New York prison cell published in Yedioth Ahronoth on Friday, Mousa Abu Marzook was asked whether he would promise to stop being active in Hamas if Israel dropped its extradition request.

"I will agree to an arrangement to be sent to another country," he said. But as for stopping his activity, he would only say: "I am still committed to working for the Palestinian cause and I will continue."
Israel has alleged that Abu Marzook, as political leader of Hamas, was responsible for attacks that killed scores of Israelis, including suicide bombers on public buses.
It demanded his extradition from the United States where he was arrested 19 months ago.
Last month, Abu Marzook dropped his court challenge to the Israeli request, in effect agreeing to be sent to Israel.
Hamas warned from Gaza it would attack Israelis if Abu Marzook was extradited. Palestinian President Yasser Arafat asked the U.S. not to send him to Israel.

On Thursday, Israeli security sources confirmed a newspaper report that Israeli, Jordanian and U.S. officials were secretly examining a deal to send Abu Marzook to Jordan in return for a promise to shun violence.
In the Yedioth interview -- Abu Marzook's first with an Israeli newspaper -- he denied he backed guerrilla attacks and stressed his political activities.

"I was not involved in any military operation," he said. "There is nobody in charge, that rules, there is no centralisation. There is no organised hierarchy in the military arm and the Israelis know that.
"The attacks were committed by cells that organised themselves and acted out of revenge. All by themselves."

Asked why he gave up on his court fight against extradition, Abu Marzook said he didn't believe he could win. Once in Israel, he didn't expect to defeat court charges against him either, he said. But he preferred to do his jail time in Israel.
"At least I'll be among other Palestinians and not isolated like here," he said.
